name: Treaty with the Pillager Band of Chippewa Indians, 1847 (Treaty of Leech Lake)
nations: Pillager Band of Ojibwe (Chippewa), today within the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe
promises: Article 3: the ceded country would be held by the United States as Indian land until the President ordered otherwise.
Article 4: for five years, annual goods (blankets, cloth, prints, twine, thread, needles, kettles, tobacco, salt and other items), with 200 beaver traps and 75 guns as a present at the first payment.

breaches.what: The Commission found the 814,500 acres ceded (Royce Area 269, between Otter Tail Lake, Long Prairie River and the Crow Wing and Leaf rivers in Minnesota) worth $425,000 on April 7, 1848, against $19,706.94 paid, and held the consideration so grossly inadequate as to be unconscionable.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Pillager Bands of Chippewa Indians v. United States, Docket 144, 32 Ind. Cl. Comm. 156 (1973)

source.title: Pillager Bands of Chippewa Indians v. United States, Docket 144, Final Award, October 25, 1973
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.quote: was so grossly inadequate as to render that consideration unconscionable

landTaken: 814,500 acres of land and water (Indian Claims Commission, 1973).
compensation: Final award of $405,293.06 to the Pillager Bands (October 25, 1973), the $425,000 value less the $19,706.94 paid; the government's claimed offsets of $1,470 were disallowed.
today: The Pillager band's descendants are part of the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe.
